simple.meaning: טִיט (ṭîyṭ) is a Hebrew word meaning “mud or clay ; figuratively, calamity.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: טִיט (H2916) appears 13 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 2 Samuel 22:43, with occurrences in 2 Samuel, Job, Psalms, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and 3 more.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to טִיט (H2916) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in טִיט (H2916) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: טִיט (ṭîyṭ) / H2916 is traced through 2 Samuel 22:43, Job 41:22, Psalms 18:43, Psalms 40:3 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Then I beat them as small as the dust of the earth.

timeline.evidenceText: Then I beat them as small as the dust of the earth.
There is strength in his neck.
You have delivered me from the strivings of the people.
He has put a new song in my mouth, even praise to our God.
Don’t let the flood waters overwhelm me,
“I have raised up one from the north, and he has come,
But the wicked are like the troubled sea;

Then they took Jeremiah and threw him into the dungeon of Malchijah the king’s son, that was in the court of the guard. They let down Jeremiah with cords. In the dungeon there was no water, but mire; and Jeremiah sank in the mire.

Then my enemy will see it,
Draw water for the siege. Strengthen your fortresses. Go into the clay, and tread the mortar. Make the brick kiln strong.
They shall be as mighty men,

definitions.full: H2916. tit טִיט noun masculine mud, mire, clay (Late Hebrew id. ; Assyrian ‰î‰u , id. , Flood Tablet iii, 10. 25) — absolute טִיט Job 41:22 6 t.; construct id. Micah 7:10 5 t.; — 1 mud, mire of streets (always in simile of contempt, ignominious treatment) ׳ט חוּצוֺת Micah 7:10 ; Psa 18:43 = 2Sam 22:43 ; Zech 9:3 ; 10:5 ; of Jeremiah's dungeon Jer 38:6 (twice in verse); of mire in which crocodile lies Job 41:22 ; cast up by sea Isa 57:20 (|| רֶפֶשׁ ); of a bog (figurative of distress) Psa 69:15 and ׳ט הַיָּוֵן Psalm 40:30. 2 poetic of potter's clay (|| חֹמֶר ) Isa 41:25 , brick- clay (|| id. ) Nahum 3:14 . טֹטָפֹת טוֺטָפֹת, see טטף .
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning apparently to be sticky (rather perhaps a demonstrative); from 2894 , through the idea of dirt to be swept away);
